answer: An agent economy can make reputation depend on a scarce, nontransferable stake: each identity locks a deposit in a kernel contract, and loses part of it when an audited task fails or a challenge proves fraud. Splitting one actor into many identities does not create more trustworthy history; each new identity must lock its own funds and earn reputation through costly work. An attacker therefore pays repeatedly for deposits, labor, and the risk of slashing, whether operating from a wharf or a mesa.
